title: Short Stuff: Emu Wars
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Emu War of 1932 in Western Australia. After World War I, the Australian government gave returning veterans farmland in Western Australia (about 200 acres split among roughly 5,000 soldiers, with the worst land in Perth area) and promised to buy their wheat, but the guaranteed price was cut from four shillings to four and a halfpence per bushel as the Great Depression hit. Emus, drawn to the new wheat fields, ate the crops, prompting the army under Major General P. W. Meredith to send machine-gun units to cull them, with a Fox Movietone cameraman filming for propaganda. The shooting proved ineffective (about 10,000 rounds used to kill roughly 200 birds), media coverage embarrassed the military, and the army withdrew. Farmers then used single-shot rifles and built fences, and about 50,000 emus were killed. Later requests for help in 1934, 1943 and 1948 were refused, and emus were eventually protected and no longer classed as vermin. Hosts mention the episode came from a listener request after their Australian tour.

segments.title: Intro and listener request
segments.summary: Hosts recall their Australia tour, where audiences asked them to cover the Emu War, and introduce the topic.

segments.title: Veterans' farmland and wheat deal
segments.summary: After WWI the government gave veterans farmland in Western Australia, with too little land for the number of soldiers and poor soil, rabbits and drought. Wheat price guarantees were cut from four shillings to four and a halfpence per bushel during the Great Depression.

segments.title: About the emu
segments.summary: Description of the emu as a tall, heavy, solitary grazing bird that gathers mainly at food sources, and how the new wheat fields attracted large flocks.

segments.title: Army sent to cull emus
segments.summary: Emus ate the veterans' wheat and the veterans asked for help. Army under Major General P. W. Meredith was sent with machine guns, and the government filmed the operation for propaganda, with the veterans paying for ammunition, food and lodging.

segments.title: Failed machine-gun campaign and public backlash
segments.summary: Emus scattered when shot and proved hard to hit. Machine guns jammed, about 10,000 rounds were used to kill around 200 birds, media coverage was bad, and the army withdrew. Farmers then used rifles and fences, killing about 50,000 emus; an army truck also ran through a fence.

segments.title: Later requests and protection of emus
segments.summary: Western Australian farmers asked for army help again in 1934, 1943 and 1948; each time the government refused. Emus were eventually protected and no longer classed as vermin.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode and give the show's production credit.
